device.name: UR5 arm with Robotiq-85/140 gripper in a PyBullet push-and-grasp scene

facts.text: ClutteredPushGrasp is the user-facing environment class
The constructor opens an in-process PyBullet connection, GUI or DIRECT, and loads the plane, the robot and a fixed box; it opens no serial, VISA, USB or network transport
step_simulation calls p.stepSimulation and sleeps the delay only when the GUI is shown
step accepts a seven-element action, asserts control_method is joint or end, calls move_ee(action[:-1], control_method) and move_gripper(action[-1]), and runs 120 simulation steps
The end-effector action is (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw, gripper_opening_length)
The interactive sliders bound x and y to -0.224..0.224, z to 0..1.0, roll and pitch to -3.14..3.14, yaw to -pi/2..pi/2 and the gripper opening to 0..0.085
read_debug_parameter returns the seven slider values in the action order
The documented user-control demo passes read_debug_parameter() and 'end' to step
step returns (observation, reward, done, info), with done true only when reward == 1
The reward becomes 1 when the box has been opened and the button pressed and the box is then closed; the joint thresholds are 1.9, -0.02 and 0.1
The observation is the camera's rgb, depth and seg arrays when a Camera is configured, plus the robot's joint observation
get_joint_obs returns the controllable joints' positions and velocities and the end-effector position
reset resets the robot and the box and returns the observation
RobotBase.reset resets the arm to the rest poses and opens the gripper; it takes no seed
UR5Robotiq85 loads ur5_robotiq_85.urdf with fixed base, eef 7, six arm dofs and gripper range 0..0.085
UR5Robotiq140 loads ur5_robotiq_140.urdf with the same eef, six arm dofs and 0..0.085 gripper range
The README lists a Gym-styled API for reinforcement learning in push-and-grasp, 6D end-effector IK with Position XYZ and Orientation RPY, and PyBullet as the only prerequisite

determinism.notes: the scene, the reset and the actions are fixed and the clone seeds no random generator; reset() restores fixed rest poses (robot.py:86-108) and the box (env.py:127-134), so the same action sequence repeats from a fresh backend.  The clone states no integer seed and exposes no get_state/set_state

gaps: one tick is one ClutteredPushGrasp.step call, which runs 120 p.stepSimulation iterations (env.py:91); the clone does not state the PyBullet physics time step, so timestep_ms is 0 (unknown) and only the step count is modelled

the action envelope is the range of the clone's interactive debug sliders (env.py:40-46); step itself does not assert those bounds and the joint-position control mode is not exposed because the clone states no joint range for it

the fake backend is a pure Python stand-in that models the tick, the last end-effector target and the observation shape but not PyBullet contacts, inverse kinematics, gravity, the box button or the reward thresholds; it was not compared with the upstream environment
camera rgb, depth and seg arrays are not modelled by the fake and the driver declares no array size or unit: a Camera-configured environment passes them through as part of the open observation object
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
